title: Restriction surjects on inertia in a Galois tower
statement:
Let $A$ be a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, and $K\subseteq L\subseteq M$ a tower such that $L/K$ and $M/K$ are Galois: algebraic, separable, and normal (every minimal polynomial of an element splits over the extension field) [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. The extensions need not be finite. Let $B\subseteq L$ and $C\subseteq M$ be the integral closures of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Choose a prime $\mathfrak r\subset C$ and set $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak r\cap B$. The groups act on the integral closures by restriction. Define
$$I_{\mathfrak r}=\{g\in\operatorname{Gal}(M/K):g\mathfrak r=\mathfrak r,\ g|_{\operatorname{Frac}(C/\mathfrak r)}=1\},\quad I_{\mathfrak q}=\{h\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/K):h\mathfrak q=\mathfrak q,\ h|_{\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak q)}=1\}.$$
Then restriction induces a surjective homomorphism $I_{\mathfrak r}\to I_{\mathfrak q}$.

proof.text: Let B = integralClosure A L, C = integralClosure A M and f : B → C be the canonical inclusion. Restriction commutes with f by AlgEquiv.restrictNormal_commutes. Applying f to the difference h(b)-b shows that the restriction of any upper inertia element lies in lower inertia. Contraction of a translated prime is the translate of its contraction, by the same equivariance applied to inverse automorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0BSX, lemma-one-orbit-geometric-galois-compare, proof; implemented directly using the profinite invariant-ring prime transitivity and quotient-lifting theorems.

proof.text: By [lem-dl-a1-galois-over-intermediate], M/L is Galois. The fixed-field theorem [lem-exc-etale-galois-fixed-field-subgroup] for the bottom field, in the equivalent form InfiniteGalois.mem_range_algebraMap_iff_fixed, shows that an element of C fixed by Gal(M/L) comes from an element y of L. Integrality descends along the injective algebra map L → M, so y belongs to B. Thus B is exactly the invariant ring of the action on C.

proof.text: The Krull topology makes Gal(M/L) profinite, using [lem-exc-galois-krull-finite-limit] and [lem-dl-a1-finite-group-limit-profinite]. Give C the discrete topology. For b in C, its orbit-map fiber through σ is the coset σ Stab(b), which is open: b is algebraic over L and its stabilizer is open in the Krull topology (Mathlib stabilizer_isOpen_of_isIntegral). These fibers give continuity of the action.

proof.text: For h in lower inertia lift h to τ in Gal(M/K) using [lem-weil-pbc-normal-subextension-automorphism-extends]. Inertia stabilizes the lower prime, so τ(r) and r have equal contraction to B. Apply prime transitivity in [lem-dl-a1-profinite-invariant-ring-primes] to the Gal(M/L)-action on C. Obtain ρ with ρ(τ(r)) = r. Then d = ρτ stabilizes r and restricts to h because ρ fixes L.

source.place: Tag 0BSX, lemma-one-orbit-geometric-galois-compare, proof; implemented directly using the profinite invariant-ring prime transitivity and quotient-lifting theorems.

proof.text: The quotient automorphism d̄ of C/r fixes B/q: its value on the class of f(b) is the class of f(h(b)), equal to the class of f(b) since h is in lower inertia. Apply quotient lifting in [lem-dl-a1-profinite-invariant-ring-primes] to obtain ε in Gal(M/L), stabilizing r and acting on C/r as d does. For every c in C, d(c)-ε(c) lies in r. Applying ε⁻¹ and using its stabilization of r gives (ε⁻¹d)(c)-c in r. Thus ε⁻¹d is in upper inertia, and its restriction is h. This proves the reverse subgroup image inclusion.
